title: Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency and abnormal procedures for the Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six with Lycoming IO-540 fuel-injected engine and constant-speed propeller. Memory items are marked. The IO-540 is fuel-injected — there is no carburetor and no carburetor heat; carburetor icing is not applicable to this engine. This checklist covers the most critical emergencies but is not exhaustive. No numeric limitations are stated; all airspeeds, power settings, and performance values must come from the specific aircraft POH. Not a substitute for regular emergency training and proficiency practice.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the Piper PA-32-301 Cherokee Six and the Lycoming IO-540 fuel-injected engine.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff

items.text: Throttle
Brakes — apply firmly to stop within remaining runway; maintain directional control
Mixture
Fuel selector
Ignition switch
Master switch
If airborne with insufficient runway remaining — land ahead; do not attempt to return to runway at low altitude; remain within 30 degrees of runway heading
items.detail: The PA-32-301 is a heavy aircraft. Aggressive maneuvering at low altitude and low airspeed following engine failure is extremely hazardous.

items.text: Flaps — if briefly airborne and landing on overrun or adjacent terrain
items.response: EXTEND AS NEEDED TO REDUCE TOUCHDOWN SPEED

items.text: Occupants — advise to brace if off-airport landing is imminent
Airspeed — establish best glide immediately
items.response: PER POH; MAINTAIN TO MAXIMIZE GLIDE RANGE

items.text: Landing area — identify suitable field; begin turn toward it
Fuel selector — switch to fullest or alternate tank
Fuel boost pump
Mixture
Ignition switch — confirm fully in BOTH position
Throttle — advance to check for engine response; assess whether power loss is partial or total
Alternate air — select ON if intake blockage or induction icing is suspected
Engine restart — if altitude and conditions permit, follow POH air-restart sequence; do not delay forced landing planning
items.response: ATTEMPTED PER POH; FORCED LANDING PLANNED SIMULTANEOUSLY

items.text: Mayday — transmit on 121.5 MHz and current ATC frequency; aircraft type, position, altitude, intentions
Transponder
If engine does not restart — proceed to Forced Landing checklist
Mixture
items.response: IDLE CUT-OFF — starve engine of fuel immediately

items.text: Fuel selector
Fuel boost pump
Throttle
Master switch — all electrical
Cabin heat and fresh air vents — close all to prevent fumes or smoke from entering cabin
If fire persists — increase airspeed in a diving descent to extinguish fire by airflow; do not exceed Vne
Mayday — if radio available before electrical shutdown; position and intentions transmitted
Forced landing — execute immediately; do not delay for restart attempts when fire is active
If fire appears to be in the induction area and engine is running — throttle: advance briefly to full to draw fire back through intake
items.response: ATTEMPT TO STARVE FIRE; SECONDS ONLY
items.detail: Only attempt while engine is turning. If the fire does not extinguish within a few seconds, proceed immediately to shutdown steps below.

items.text: Mixture
Fuel selector
Fuel boost pump
Ignition switch
Master switch
All occupants — evacuate immediately via cabin door and aft door; move well clear upwind of aircraft
Fire extinguisher — approach from upwind; aim at base of fire; do not place yourself between fire and fuel tanks
Emergency services
Master switch
Avionics master switch
All individual electrical switches
Fresh air vents — open to clear smoke; do not use cabin heat
Fire extinguisher — if smoke or flame persists
items.response: USE HALON OR CO2 TYPE; NOT WATER

items.text: If fire appears extinguished — restore one switch at a time to isolate the offending circuit
items.response: RESTORED ONE AT A TIME; FAULTED CIRCUIT IDENTIFIED AND LEFT OFF

items.text: Minimum avionics for navigation and communication — restore only essentials
Mayday — on 121.5 if radio can be restored; advise smoke in cockpit
Land at nearest suitable airport
Oil pressure gauge — verify reading; cross-check oil temperature; rising CHT and oil temp alongside zero pressure confirms actual loss versus gauge failure
items.response: ACTUAL LOSS CONFIRMED OR GAUGE FAILURE IDENTIFIED

items.text: Power — reduce to minimum consistent with continued controlled flight
Landing area — select nearest suitable field; begin precautionary landing planning; engine seizure may be imminent without warning
Mayday — transmit on 121.5 MHz; aircraft type, position, altitude, oil pressure emergency declared
Engine instruments — monitor CHT and oil temperature continuously for rapid rise indicating imminent seizure
Land without delay — engine failure without warning may follow total oil loss

sections.title: Induction Air Blockage / Alternate Air
sections.condition: Unexplained power loss; suspected induction filter icing in visible moisture near freezing temperatures

items.text: The IO-540 is fuel-injected and has no carburetor — carburetor ice is not a hazard. However, the induction air filter can ice over in visible moisture near freezing temperatures, causing unexplained power loss. The alternate air control bypasses the filtered intake and draws warm unfiltered air from inside the cowling.
Alternate air control
items.response: ON — bypasses blocked or iced induction filter

items.text: Power response — expect partial restoration; brief roughness as any accumulated ice ingests
items.response: PARTIAL RESTORATION EXPECTED; ROUGHNESS NORMAL AND TRANSIENT

items.text: Mixture — adjust as needed for changed induction airflow
When clear of icing conditions — return alternate air to normal
Airspeed — establish best glide and maintain; adjust for aircraft weight if required by POH
Landing area — select longest available surface oriented as close into wind as possible; avoid wires, trees, structures, and ditches
Mayday — transmit on 121.5 MHz and current frequency; aircraft type, position, altitude, souls on board, nature of emergency
Transponder
Fuel selector
Fuel boost pump
Mixture
Ignition switch
Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants; tighten and brief brace position
Cabin doors — both cabin door and aft baggage door unlatched before touchdown to prevent jamming in a deformed airframe
Master switch — retain for flap operation; OFF immediately before touchdown
Flaps — deploy on final to increase descent angle and reduce touchdown speed; adjust aim point accordingly
Touchdown — aim for far end of selected surface; land at minimum controllable airspeed; apply brakes aggressively after touchdown
items.response: MINIMUM SPEED; MAXIMUM BRAKING AFTER TOUCHDOWN
